body: Or what's the browserify way for this?

Yeah I guess, strictly speaking it should throw an error, and you should use `try/catch` to check for the existence of the module.

But I guess webpack won't change this?

Mhmmm returning an empty object doesn't make sense at all. Or does anybody know a use-case where it is useful?

Using `try/catch` isn't nice either, but afaik it's the de-facto standard to check for [`optionalDependencies`](https://www.npmjs.org/doc/files/package.json.html#optionaldependencies) in node. And in this case the `fs`-module seems to be an optional dependency. What do you think @sokra ?

And btw: Do you think it would be possible to provide a fs shim with the context replacement plugin?

I don't think providing a shim for `fs` makes sense. If something is meant to be used in the browser and in node, then that thing just needs to know whether `fs` is there or not, as it's only going to do some extra stuff in node. Shiming it out might cause unintended consequences and cause the code to break in weir ways.

Hmm.. looks like the commit https://github.com/webpack/webpack/commit/3364a26967e9ca360ffcca82fecb63a74d7cbc27 broke it...

`require("fs")` should throw...

How can we bundle a module which does have code that requires fs for the node-specific parts now? The module makes sure it requires fs only in a node-context, but webpack now fails to compile it at all...
browserify uses an empty module here: https://github.com/substack/node-browserify/blob/47c6933e711567de761c73fe81165223c7873433/lib/builtins.js#L12
@c089 best way is to use the `browser` field in the `package.json` and ignore `fs`... i. e. `"browser": { "fs": false }`

body:
FWIW: I've tried all the workarounds including setting `"browser": { "fs": false }` in package.json but without success.

Found a [SO post](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/25565558/how-have-webpack-skip-a-module-if-it-doesnt-exist) that suggested switching to Marked and now everything just works. This is probably an issue that is unique to Showdown. Webpack works as expected for me.

issue.title: Replace Gulp with Webpack
issue.body:
## Use Webpack instead of Gulp for bundling css and javascript
### Testing ACs
1. The app runs just like it used to.
### Dev ACs
1. Gulp is gone
2. Webpack builds app.js file
3. Webpack builds app.css file
4. Webpack rebuilds js and css without reloading the page
5. Webpack "emits" media files to the right directory
6. Environment variable replacing works
7. Sourcemaps work
8. JShint and JSXhint run on appropriate files; Webpack shows jshint warnings in the terminal
9. Webpack and Hot Loader start with `npm start`
10. Production builds can be created with `npm run dist`
### Notes
- Biggest difference from the gulp build is that media files will be included with their full path

issue.title: _fs.readFileSync is not a function

repository.name: sheetjs
repository.description: 📗 SheetJS Spreadsheet Data Toolkit -- New home https://git.sheetjs.com/SheetJS/sheetjs

issue.body:
Having difficulty reading XLSX files in the browser.
1. `npm install --save xlsx`
2. Ensure and `xlsx` folder is present in `/node_modules`
3. In my JS file, add the following:

```
import XLSX  from `xlsx`;
var workbook = XLSX.readFile('../../data/test.xlsx');
```

Immediately hit the error:

> xlsx.js:11387 Uncaught TypeError: _fs.readFileSync is not a function

And yet if I transition the `import` statement to something more ES5 friendly (`require`), the application can't even locate the `XLSX` library anymore, which is confusing because it's _in_ /node_modules:

```
if(typeof require !== 'undefined') XLSX = require('xlsx');
var workbook = XLSX.readFile('../../data/test.xlsx');
```

 Immediately hit the error:

> my-test-file.jsx:55 Uncaught ReferenceError: XLSX is not defined

I added the following to my webpack per some previous open issues, however I didn't see a decent explanation for why this is required:

> ```
> resolve: {
>     extensions: ['', '.js', '.jsx', '.json']
> },
> node: {
>     fs: 'empty'
> },
> ```
